solution.p: A lines standard form is Ax+By=C\text{.} We need to move x and y terms to the same side of the equal sign. \begin{aligned} {y}\amp={\frac{6}{7}x+6}\\ \multiplyleft{7}{y}\amp=\multiplyleft{7}\left({\frac{6}{7}x+6}\right)\\ 7y\amp=7\left( \frac{6}{7}x \right)+7(6)\\ 7y\amp=6x+42\\ 7y\subtractright{6x}\amp=6x+42\subtractright{6x}\\ {-6x+7y}\amp=42\\ \multiplyleft{-1}({-6x+7y})\amp=\multiplyleft{-1}(42)\\ {6x-7y}\amp=-42 \end{aligned} Note that {-6x+7y}=42 is already in standard form, but its better to get rid of the leading negative sign in an equation.
